meaning: to watch someone or something carefully
example: Please keep an eye on my bag while I buy a ticket.
origin: Likely comes from the idea of keeping your eye fixed on a person or object so that it does not disappear or get taken.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to close your eyes and rest
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This describes sleeping or resting, but the idiom is about paying close attention with your eyes open.
This is the opposite of the idiom, which means continuing to look carefully.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to hit someone in the face
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This describes physical violence, which has nothing to do with watching or paying attention.

explanation: 'Keep an eye on' uses the word 'eye' to mean careful watching. It is common in everyday English, for example when asking someone to look after your things.
